Tara (PM): Quick sync — we need to re-negotiate the launch slice after the capacity update from infra. Customers in pilot expect embeddings at scale.
Kevin (Eng): Ack. What are the hard constraints from CS?
Sam (CS): Two paying pilots. They need 99% of requests under 200ms p50 and bulk embeddings for nightly jobs (<=10M tokens/day).
Maya (Infra): Current Dedicated pool capacity drops by ~30% next week due to GPU maintenance windows. Autoscale handles bursts but sustained nightly jobs will queue.
Tara (PM): So options: 1) trim feature set to avoid heavy nightly embeddings 2) prioritize embedding route to Dedicated with reserved slots 3) delay rollout a week. Thoughts?
Kevin (Eng): Prefer 2 if we can reserve slots — avoids changing UX. But reserved slots mean commit and budget.
Sam (CS): Pilots will pay for reserved capacity if we can guarantee latency SLA. I can push on contracts but need clear cut list of what we keep.
Linh (Design): If we trim, we should hide batch-upload in the pilot UI rather than remove embeddings completely. Less churn.
Maya (Infra): Reservation proposal: allocate 2x GPUs for 72 hours nightly -> handles 10M tokens with headroom. Requires Dedicated config change + canary.
Tara (PM): Can we do a staged rollout: reserve capacity for pilot customers only, limit batch-upload to pilot orgs, full public rollout later?
Kevin (Eng): Yes — we can gate by org flag. Implementation: feature flag + routing rule to Dedicated pool. Rough ETA 3 days to land gate + 1 day canary.
Maya (Infra): We'll need scheduled job kickoff window and monitoring. I'll add a temporary alert for queue depth and token/sec.
Tara (PM): Great. Tradeoffs: no UI change for pilots, public users see batch-upload hidden. Risk: ops overhead for reservation.
Sam (CS): I'll inform customers and get verbal OK; will confirm signed commits by EOD tomorrow.
Kevin (Eng): For rollout safety, can we add fallback to online small-batch embedding model if queue grows?
Maya (Infra): Yes — routing policy can fall back to quantized model with higher latency but lower cost. We'll auto-failover at queue > 80%.
Tara (PM): Acceptance criteria for pilot slice: 1) pilot orgs can ingest batches up to 10M tokens/night 2) p50 <=200ms for single-request path 3) alerting on queue >50% done 4) rollback plan documented.
Kevin (Eng): Adding short checklist in PR: code flag, routing, fallback, tests, canary deploy script.
Linh (Design): I'll update the pilot UI copy to say "pilot batch uploads enabled" and hide for public.
Sam (CS): Customer comms draft: "We reserved capacity for your pilot to ensure performance; we'll confirm SLA in writing once contracts are final."
Tara (PM): Timing: aim to ship reserved-gate + canary by Thu EOD. If contracts delayed, fallback is to trim nightly batch size and delay public.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-gate/embeddings-reserved -> staging at 1798881260
Kevin (Eng): Noted staging deploy. Will watch metrics and iterate.
Maya (Infra): I'll set up dashboard panels: queue depth, token/sec, p50/p95 latency for both pools.
Tara (PM): Thanks. Action owners: Kevin - feature flag + fallback (3 days), Maya - infra reservation + dashboard (2 days), Linh - UI copy (1 day), Sam - customer sign-off (EOD tomorrow).
Sam (CS): Will ping customers now.
Tara (PM): If any blocker pops up, call a quick huddle. :thumbsup:
Kevin (Eng): Thanks — will update thread with PR links and canary results.
Maya (Infra): Deploy metrics look good on canary, queue stable.
Kevin (Eng): Canary posted: https://ci/reports/embeddings-canary-179888 -> p50 180ms, nightly sim within limits.
Sam (CS): Customers verbally OK, awaiting contracts.
Tara (PM): Closing for now; will reopen if contract or performance issues surface.
